nodes.label: Initiation and Pre-Trial Disposition
nodes.summary: Modes of initiation, offence classification, committal/transfer, discharge, time limits, and abuse of process.

nodes.label: Modes of Initiation
nodes.summary: Information/complaint (Cap 227 ss.8, 26) for summary trial. Charge sheet (Cap 221 s.14A) for indictable offences filed at magistracy; becomes indictment after transfer or filing in CFI/DC. Prosecution by Secretary for Justice: absolute discretion subject to judicial review only in exceptional circumstances.

nodes.label: Magistrates Ordinance (Cap 227) s.8
nodes.summary: Information/complaint for summary trial.

nodes.label: Magistrates Ordinance (Cap 227) s.26
nodes.summary: Time limit for laying information: 6 months for summary offences.

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) s.14A
nodes.summary: Charge sheet for indictable offences; classification of offences as summary/indictable/either way.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Cheung Tsz Wan (2009) 12 HKCFAR 520
nodes.summary: Prosecutorial discretion; judicial review only in exceptional circumstances. Reaffirmation of burden for stay.

nodes.label: Classification of Offences
nodes.summary: Summary only: triable only in Magistrates' Court. Indictable only: must go to CFI (or DC after transfer). Either way: may be tried summarily or on indictment, depending on prosecution election and magistrate's view (Cap 221 s.14A).

nodes.label: HKSAR v Chan Tai Sum (2021)
nodes.summary: Classification under s.14A; whether offence is summary or indictable.

nodes.label: Committal / Transfer Route
nodes.summary: Magistrates' committal for CFI trial: paper committal under Cap 221 Part II (ss.79A-79H) for indictable only offences. Transfer to District Court under Cap 221 s.77C: Secretary for Justice may apply; magistrate orders transfer if conditions met.

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) ss.79A-79H
nodes.summary: Paper committal procedure for indictable only offences to CFI.

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) s.77C
nodes.summary: Transfer to District Court; Secretary for Justice may apply.

nodes.label: Discharge Before Trial / Stay for Abuse of Process
nodes.summary: Magistrate may discharge defendant if insufficient evidence at committal or if no case. Abuse of process/stay: rare remedy where fair trial impossible or proceedings an affront to justice. Stay only exceptional; prosecution misconduct alone not enough if fair trial possible.

nodes.label: R v Holgate (No 1) (comparative)
nodes.summary: Burden on applicant for stay.

nodes.label: Time Limits / Delay
nodes.summary: Statute of limitations: some offences have time limits for laying information (e.g. summary offences: 6 months, Cap 227 s.26). Indictable offences generally no time limit, but delay causing prejudice may ground stay.

nodes.label: Stay Flow: Identify Alleged Abuse
nodes.summary: Step 1: Identify alleged abuse of process (prosecutorial misconduct, delay, unfairness).

nodes.label: Stay Flow: Assess Fair Trial Possibility
nodes.summary: Step 2: Is a fair trial still possible? If yes, stay rarely granted.

nodes.label: Stay Flow: Exceptional Circumstances
nodes.summary: Step 3: Are the circumstances exceptional? Stay is a rare remedy.

nodes.label: Stay Flow: Applicant Burden
nodes.summary: Step 4: Applicant bears burden of establishing grounds for stay.

nodes.label: Stay Flow: Court Decision or Lesser Remedy
nodes.summary: Step 5: Court considers stay or lesser remedy (adjournment, exclusion of evidence).

nodes.label: Stay Flow: Appeal Route
nodes.summary: Step 6: Appeal route if stay granted or refused.
